title: Persistence of bilateral swing asymmetry did not add reliable cross-database Parkinson discrimination
abstract: Existing public gait recordings were used to test whether serial persistence of left–right swing-time asymmetry contains incremental Parkinson disease information. Fixed standardized penalized logistic models trained on 30 gaitndd participants were evaluated without target fitting in 126 gaitpdb participants. Adding lag-one correlation of log swing-time ratios to demographics, stride mean and variability, swing fraction and asymmetry summaries changed target Brier score from 0.210942 to 0.211372; paired difference 0.000430, 95% interval [-0.000965759712625701, 0.0018698117383644426]. Source leave-one-out prediction also worsened. A two-sample refitting bootstrap included zero. A shorter-window sensitivity improved target prediction, so the result does not establish universal absence of signal. This is a negative incremental-prediction test under one harmonization, not a clinical biomarker validation. Small age-confounded discovery, force-threshold selection and unavailable participant linkage constrain interpretation. Author self-checks identified contradictory-label duplicate target files, excluded explicitly although not retained by the primary window.
